clue.text: Confuse medical department, showing an abnormal leg

parts.note: ENT is the hospital department for ear, nose and throat

indicators.note: abnormal says the three letters of leg are not in their usual order

explanation.surface: A doctor in the ear, nose and throat unit is baffled by a patient whose leg looks odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abnormal' rearranges only the three letters of 'leg'; ENT is the usual hospital shorthand for ear, nose and throat.
explanation.definitionFit: To entangle someone is to muddle or involve them confusingly, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Upright soldier appearing very strong in the old image

indicators.note: in a down clue, upright means the letters climb, so the whole is read bottom to top
in puts the soldier and the strong letters inside the old word

parts.note: ye is an old form of the
GI is an American soldier
FF is fortissimo in music, very loud or strong

explanation.surface: An upstanding soldier looks mighty in an old picture.
explanation.walkthrough: GIFF goes inside YE to make YGIFFE; 'Upright' turns it all upward.
explanation.definitionFit: An effigy is a likeness or image of a person, often a carving or dummy.

clue.text: Working extra shift, financial statement's needed

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: a turn is a shift of work

explanation.surface: Doing an extra shift at work means filing more paperwork for the taxman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' rearranges EXTRA into TAXRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tax return is the form declaring income and liabilities to the tax authority.

clue.text: Once called associate when stripping a turkey

parts.note: ne, the masculine of nee, means formerly called

indicators.note: stripping means taking off, so the a is removed from the ally

parts.note: an ally is an associate

explanation.surface: A former associate is busy stripping and plucking a turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turkey' looks like a bird but is a dud or fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A nelly is old British slang for a silly person, as is turkey for a fool.

clue.text: See bachelor in depression, appealing

parts.note: lo means see, as in lo and behold

indicators.note: in puts the bachelor letter inside the valley

parts.note: a vale is a valley, a depression in the land

explanation.surface: Look at the single man feeling low: rather endearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' suggests low spirits but is a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovable means charming or endearing, as appealing does.

clue.text: Progressively raise setter, regularly clipping dog

indicators.note: clipping means fastening on to, so the two parts are joined side by side
regularly takes every other letter of setter, starting with the first

parts.note: a pup is a young dog

explanation.surface: A setter dog has its coat trimmed at regular intervals while someone breeds them up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clipping' looks like a trim, but here it means attaching: STE is clipped on to PUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To step something up is a phrasal verb for increasing it stage by stage.

clue.text: Test about half of them on sport

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the test word goes around the other piece

parts.note: a trial is a test

indicators.note: half of takes the first two of the four letters in them

explanation.surface: A sporting test is held about half of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes the test word wrap around the half of 'them'; 'on' is then simply taken as it stands.
explanation.definitionFit: A triathlon is an endurance sport of swimming, cycling and running.

clue.text: Crown hearing for offence

indicators.note: hearing says the word is heard spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: a crown or summit is a peak

explanation.surface: A court hearing over an offence against the Crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crown' and 'offence' suggest a criminal trial; offence here means taking umbrage.
explanation.definitionFit: Pique is wounded pride, a fit of resentment, as in taking offence.

clue.text: Standing near French cat that's tailless

parts.note: pres is the French for near

indicators.note: tailless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a tiger is a big cat

explanation.surface: A tailless French cat stands nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Prestige is status or reputation, as one's standing in society.

clue.text: Plant kiss on female, given ring that's put on hand

indicators.note: given here means having something put into it, so the round letter goes between the other two
on means placed after, so the kiss follows the female letter

parts.note: X is the cross used for a kiss at the end of a letter
O is ring-shaped
a glove is worn on the hand

explanation.surface: A romantic plants a kiss on a woman and gives her a ring for her finger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' places O between F and X. 'Plant' looks like a verb (plant a kiss) but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The foxglove is a tall flowering garden plant, source of digitalis.

clue.text: Some rabbis question fish dish

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some rabbis raise doubts about whether a particular seafood dish is permitted.
explanation.definitionFit: A bisque is a rich creamy soup, classically made from shellfish such as lobster.

clue.text: Cornish sailor's mop on board

parts.note: Cornwall is in the south-west of England, abbreviated SW
AB is an able seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor from Cornwall swabs the deck of the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A swab is a mop used to clean a ship's decks.

clue.text: Obsessive about tablets perhaps, European runs off, back to pharmacy

indicators.note: off means taken away, so the runs letter leaves the European

parts.note: a Greek is a European
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: back to picks the final letter of pharmacy

explanation.surface: A European fixated on medicine runs off and then heads back to the chemist's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tablets' suggests pills, but here it means tablet computers, the kind of gadget a techie fusses over.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone geeky is obsessively enthusiastic about technology, such as tablet computers.

clue.text: Runners once seen here bend and stretch, leaving clubhouse, conserving energy

parts.note: to bow is to bend

indicators.note: conserving means holding something inside
leaving means those letters depart from the word stretch

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for clubhouse
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Athletes bend and stretch as they leave the clubhouse, saving their energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' strips the clubhouse letters to give STRET, which 'conserving' wraps round E. The Bow Street Runners were London's early police force, based at Bow Street magistrates' court.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bow Street Runners, an eighteenth-century London constabulary, were based at that street's court.

clue.text: Clergyman's worried by scoundrel

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible man
ate, as in what's eating you, means worried or troubled

explanation.surface: A vicar is troubled by some villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried by scoundrel' puts ATE beside CUR, the scoundrel first.
explanation.definitionFit: A curate is an assistant member of the clergy in a parish.

clue.text: Some of perfume, a shade over one thousand dollars, upset gent

indicators.note: in a down clue over means above, so this comes first

parts.note: amber is a shade of yellow-orange
G stands for a grand, a thousand dollars

indicators.note: upset means turned upside down, so in a down clue the word runs upwards

parts.note: sir is a gentleman's title

explanation.surface: A gent upset at paying a thousand dollars for a tiny drop of scent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SIR into RIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambergris, a waxy secretion from sperm whales, is a traditional ingredient used to fix perfumes.

clue.text: Command Father to reject symbol of this country

parts.note: a papal bull is an edict, a command

indicators.note: to reject means turning back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: God the Father

explanation.surface: An order tells the head of the family to disown the national emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: The FT is a British paper, so 'this country' is Britain, whose emblem is the bulldog, linked with John Bull and Churchill.
explanation.definitionFit: The bulldog is a traditional emblem of British tenacity.

clue.text: Doctor hides odd contrary crush on old band leader

indicators.note: hides means keeps out of sight inside, so the rest goes within the doctor
in a down clue on means placed above, so this comes before the next piece

parts.note: rum means odd or strange

indicators.note: contrary means the other way round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a jam is a crush of people

explanation.surface: A doctor conceals a strange, perverse infatuation with an old bandleader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrary' turns JAM into MAJ; DR 'hides' RUM, MAJ and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A drum major leads a marching band, setting the pace with a mace.

clue.text: Clothing outlet overflows ahead of spring

indicators.note: in a down clue ahead of means placed above, so this comes first

parts.note: slops means spills over
a hop is a spring or jump

explanation.surface: A clothes shop's stock overflows ahead of the spring season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season but is a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: A slop shop sold cheap ready-made clothing, historically to sailors.

clue.text: Pine crook that was used as a weapon

definitions.text: that was used as a weapon
definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for a thing once used to fight

parts.note: to pine is to long for
a crook is a bend, as is a bow

explanation.surface: A shepherd's crook made of pine was once wielded as a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a descriptive phrase: the thing that was used as a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: The longbow was the English archer's medieval weapon, as at Agincourt.

clue.text: Trick the Italian into playing partners at bridge

indicators.note: into says one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: West and East are partners in bridge
il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: Someone cheats an Italian into playing as a bridge partner.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four seats are North, South, East and West, with opposite seats in partnership.
explanation.definitionFit: A wile is a cunning ruse, a trick.

clue.text: Language that's evident in butcher's?

definitions.meaning: a ... is a language, as in mother ...
a butcher sells ox ... as a cut of meat

explanation.surface: Some salty talk can be heard in the butcher's shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butcher's' also hints at rhyming slang (butcher's hook, a look), but here it is simply the meat shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue means both a spoken language and an offal cut on sale at a butcher's.

clue.text: Spanish cuisine sustains one business which elevates dessert

indicators.note: sustains means holds up from within, so the rest sits inside

parts.note: a tapa is a Spanish snack
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: in a down clue elevates means raising, so the word reads upwards

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: A firm that serves Spanish food keeps going on the strength of its desserts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'which elevates' turns CO into OC.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapioca, from cassava starch, is made into a milk pudding, a classic British school dessert.

clue.text: Sort of camera capturing variable geological feature

indicators.note: capturing means holding inside

parts.note: Canon is a camera brand
Y is a mathematical variable

explanation.surface: A camera captures a changing view of a natural landform.
explanation.definitionFit: A canyon is a deep gorge cut by a river, a landform.

clue.text: Sun possibly caught brass item on office desk?

parts.note: The Sun is a British newspaper, so an example of a paper
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
brass and lip both mean cheek or impudence

explanation.surface: A sunny day caught a brass ornament on someone's office desk.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A paperclip is a small bent-wire fastener kept among office stationery.

clue.text: Dash back, halfway into Penzance, for takeaway at Luigi's?

indicators.note: back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: to zip is to dash

indicators.note: halfway into takes the two letters in the very middle of Penzance

explanation.surface: Someone dashes back from Penzance to fetch an Italian takeaway.
explanation.walkthrough: Penzance is a town in Cornwall. 'Luigi's' suggests an Italian restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: A pizza is the classic Italian takeaway, the kind an Italian named Luigi might run.

clue.text: Classical character's publication diverted graduate

indicators.note: diverted means turned the other way, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a mag is a magazine, a publication
MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: A figure from the classics has a magazine diverted to a graduate.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamma is the third letter of the Greek alphabet, a character of a classical language.

clue.text: Crunch good bit of bacon

parts.note: the rind is the tough skin on a rasher of bacon

explanation.surface: Biting into crunchy good bacon.
explanation.definitionFit: To grind is to crush or crunch, as teeth or a mill do.

clue.text: Difficult to restrain extremists displaying menace

indicators.note: to restrain means to hold in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: hard means difficult
A and Z are the extremes of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Extremists are hard to hold back and pose a threat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremists' looks political but means the two extreme letters of the alphabet, A to Z.
explanation.definitionFit: A hazard is a danger or threat, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Dandy to go off with fashionable bird

parts.note: to pop is to go off, as a gun or balloon does
in means fashionable
a jay is a bird of the crow family

explanation.surface: A fop goes off with a stylish bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A popinjay is a vain, showily dressed man, a fop.

clue.text: What flock might do to breed with tup finally

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of tup

parts.note: to raise animals is to breed them

explanation.surface: Sheep breeding needs a ram, a tup, to finish the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flock' suggests sheep, as does 'tup' (a ram), but the flock is a church congregation praising God.
explanation.definitionFit: A church's flock, its congregation, gathers to worship and laud God.

clue.text: Outsiders in media almost ring high-ranking official

parts.note: the outer letters of media are M and A, written out as the words M and A

indicators.note: almost drops the last letter of the word ring

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Media outsiders nearly ring a top bureaucrat.
explanation.walkthrough: The outsiders of 'media' are M AND A, the joining word kept in.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandarin is a senior civil servant, after the officials of imperial China.
